stories.headline: Rescuers search for survivors after Tibet earthquake kills 16, injures 76
stories.title: Rescuers search for survivors after Tibet earthquake kills 16, injures 76
stories.summary: Rescuers combed through a remote area in the Chinese region of Tibet on Friday after a magnitude 7 earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured 76 and collapsed hundreds of homes, according to Chinese state media. The disaster struck Nagqu, a city north of Tibet's capital Lhasa that is some 4,800 metres (15,748 feet) above sea level, on Thursday. At least 339 homes collapsed, and officials told journalists they were concerned about further building collapses from aftershocks, as well as casualties from rockslides. China's national broadcaster CCTV aired footage on Friday showing collapsed houses and shattered stone walls in Nagqu. More than 12,000 residents in the region were evacuated, with additional shelters under construction, China's official news agency Xinhua reported. No one was reported missing in Baqen County in Nagqu, where the earthquake struck. Search and rescue efforts are complicated by the geography and low temperatures, officials said. stories.headline: Trump claims 250% tariff threat stopped India-Pakistan war
stories.title: Trump claims 250% tariff threat stopped India-Pakistan war
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Donald Trump says he threatened India and Pakistan with 250% tariffs to stop fighting, but India maintains the ceasefire followed a Pakistani military request.

US President Donald Trump has once again claimed that his threat to impose 250 per cent tariffs on India and Pakistan helped bring their military confrontation to an end, renewing a claim that New Delhi has repeatedly disputed.
Speaking at a campaign rally, Trump said he warned both nuclear-armed neighbours that they would lose access to trade with the United States if they continued fighting.
“You stop India and Pakistan, two nuclear nations,” Trump said, describing what he portrayed as a direct intervention to prevent further escalation.
He claimed that he threatened both countries with tariffs of 250 per cent, adding that the warning angered their leadership but eventually stopped the fighting.
“They got very upset, very angry; they stopped shooting, and the war was over,” Trump said.
He also repeated his claim that 11 aircraft had been shot down during the confrontation.
Trump went on to cite his claimed diplomatic interventions as evidence of his role in resolving international conflicts, expressing frustration that he had not received the Nobel Peace Prize.

India has consistently rejected Trump's account of the ceasefire, maintaining that the understanding to stop military action was reached through direct military communication between the two countries.
According to India's stated position, Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) contacted his Indian counterpart to request a halt to hostilities.
New Delhi has also disputed Trump's claim about 11 aircraft being shot down.
The disagreement over the ceasefire's origins has persisted despite Trump's repeated assertions that his trade threats helped end the confrontation.

stories.headline: Cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal, fishermen put on alert
stories.title: Cyclone threat looms over Bay of Bengal, fishermen put on alert
stories.summary: Chennai, Oct 24 : Fishermen were on Saturday advised against venturing into the open sea for five days from Sunday as a cyclonic storm is expected to develop over the Bay of Bengal, according to a weather advisory. Several districts of Tamil Nadu are also likely to receive heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds. The Chennai weather department, in its bulletin, said a weather system over the Comorin region and adjoining southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala on October 22 had shifted towards the southeastern Arabian Sea and neighbouring Lakshadweep region by 8.30 a.m. on October 23. An associated atmospheric trough extending towards the northern Tamil Nadu coast through Kerala, at about 1.5 kms above sea level, was influencing rainfall across the region. For October 24, heavy rain was forecast at isolated places in Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari districts and the hill areas of Coimbatore, the Nilgiris and Theni. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40–50 kmph were also predicted. Rain was expected across several other districts, including Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruchirappalli, Tenkasi, Madurai, Dindigul, Virudhunagar and Tiruppur. Chennai and its neighbouring districts, the delta region, Puducherry and Karaikal were also expected to experience showers. On October 25, isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Perambalur, Ariyalur and Tiruchirappalli. Thunderstorms and gusty winds may accompany rainfall in Sivaganga, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Tirupattur, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Vellore and Ranipet, besides several western and northern districts. Rain is also forecast for Chennai, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Tiruvallur, Cuddalore and parts of the Cauvery delta. The department forecast a further spell of intense rain on October 26, with isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall likely in the Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Theni, Madurai, Sivaganga, Ramanathapuram and Pudukkottai. Other districts, including Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Karur, Tiruppur, Dindigul and Virudhunagar, could also receive heavy showers. Rain accompanied by thunder, lightning and winds of 40–50 kmph is expected in parts of Thoothukudi, Perambalur, Ariyalur, Kallakurichi, Cuddalore and Tiruvannamalai, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal. Elsewhere in Tamil Nadu, moderate rainfall is likely at varying numbers of locations during the three-day forecast period. The five-day warning for fishermen begins on Sunday and extends through Thursday, October 29. The advisory links the restriction to the anticipated development of the Bay of Bengal weather system. —IANS

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab may approach Odisha coast; Kerala puts 10 districts under orange alert
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab may approach Odisha coast; Kerala puts 10 districts under orange alert
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The IMD has warned that Cyclone Arnab could develop over the Bay of Bengal by October 26, with winds gusting up to 90 kmph and a possible approach towards the Andhra Pradesh–Odisha coast.
Meanwhile, 10 Kerala districts are under an orange alert for heavy rain on October 24.

New Delhi: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned that a cyclonic storm could develop over the Bay of Bengal by October 26 and move towards the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast around October 28.
Meanwhile, Kerala is expected to experience continued heavy rainfall, with orange alerts issued in 10 districts on Saturday, October 24.
The IMD has forecast the development of a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26.

The weather system, which was identified as a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday, October 23, is expected to intensify into a depression on October 24 before strengthening further.

According to the forecast, the system could develop into a cyclonic storm by October 26 and move west-northwestwards towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the following two days.
If the system develops into a cyclone, it will be named Arnab, a name proposed by Bangladesh.
IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said wind speeds could reach 70–80 kmph, with gusts of up to 90 kmph, from the morning of October 26.
Wind speeds and the storm's intensity could increase as the system develops.
The exact path and landfall location have not yet been confirmed.
Odisha authorities said greater clarity on the system's movement could emerge by Saturday.

stories.headline: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.title: Cabinet Sub-Committee seeks to draw up department-wise plan to tackle El Nino induced drought conditions
stories.summary: 358 mandals provisionally identified as drought-affected based on rainfall, crop coverage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Cabinet Sub-Committee on Drought and El Nino conditions chaired by Deputy Chief Minister M. Bhatti Vikramarka on Friday resolved to prepare a comprehensive and department-wise action plan to tackle the drought caused by El Nino conditions.

The plans will focus on safeguarding supply of water for drinking and irrigation and ensuring uninterrupted electricity, agricultural support and rural employment so that people do not face hardships in the coming days.

The first meeting of the Cabinet Sub-Committee, constituted to review the drought and El Nino situation in the State and recommend appropriate measures to the government, was held here on Friday (October 23).
The meeting primarily discussed the impact of El Nino and drought in various parts of the State, water availability, relief measures for farmers and future action plans.

Sub-Committee members and Ministers N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, D. Seethakka, Tummala Nageswara Rao and Vakiti Srihari along with Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju and secretaries of the concerned departments attended the meeting.
Mr. Vikramarka asked the officials to scientifically assess drought conditions and examine the mandals eligible for declaration as drought-affected areas under the prescribed guidelines.
He stressed that the government’s priority was to minimise the impact of drought and ensure timely delivery of necessary assistance to people through coordinated efforts.
He instructed officials to assess not only areas already experiencing severe drought but also mandals where the drought impact exceeds 20%.
An advance assessment of the likely impact of drought on various sectors would help the government provide timely assistance to those in need, he said.
He suggested that every department identify the challenges and prepare a clear action plan to address them.
He asked the officials to anticipate challenges in the power sector arising from El Nino conditions and take measures in advance.
Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy asked the District Collectors to conduct weekly review meetings with the officials concerned to monitor the measures being implemented to address the drought conditions.

stories.headline: Gold, silver prices drop sharply as oil prices surge
stories.title: Gold, silver prices drop sharply as oil prices surge
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 24 : Gold prices dipped 3.28 per cent on a weekly basis, while silver prices declined 7.83 per cent this week, as rising crude oil prices heightened inflation fears. The rising inflation concerns reinforced expectations that global interest rates will stay higher for longer, prompting a wave of selling across precious‑metals markets. On Friday, MCX gold futures expiring December declined 0.81 per cent while MCX silver futures for December shed 1.75 per cent. Gold futures stood at Rs 1,42,150, while silver futures stood at Rs 1,96,100 per kg. Gold saw its steepest weekly decline since June and slipped below the psychologically important $4,000 per ounce level for the first time since mid-July, analysts said. The selloff in silver intensified over weakness in US technology stocks, particularly AI-linked companies, which triggered margin calls and forced investors to liquidate precious-metal holdings. Meanwhile, crude oil surged to multi-month highs following renewed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes, while the Indian rupee surrendered its early-week gains amid rising oil prices and renewed dollar demand. However, lower prices encouraged physical gold purchases in India during the Dussehra festival, providing some underlying demand support, while Chinese jewellery demand remained subdued. Market participants forecast that precious metals could remain under pressure if elevated energy prices reinforce inflation concerns and expectations of tighter monetary policy. However, physical demand and any moderation in bond yields could offer support following the recent correction, they said. Markets largely expect the US Fed to keep interest rates unchanged at the October 27–28 policy meeting, but expectations of another rate hike in December remain elevated, with traders pricing approximately a 78 per cent probability. Investors are also awaiting the US Personal Consumption Expenditures report next week for additional guidance on inflation and future interest-rate decisions. Immediate resistance for Comex Gold is placed at $4,070–$4,100 zone, while support lies at $3,970–$4,000 zone, analysts said. For MCX Gold, immediate resistance is placed at Rs 1,43,000–Rs 1,43,700 zone, while the support lies at Rs 1,40,000–Rs 1,41,000, they added. —IANS aar/na

stories.headline: India set to defend blind cricket Asia Cup title with 17-member squad
stories.title: India set to defend blind cricket Asia Cup title with 17-member squad
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 25 : India have announced a 17-member squad for the second Men’s Blind Cricket Asia Cup, scheduled to be held in Dhaka from November 15 to 20, as the defending champions prepare to retain their title after a decade-long gap in the tournament. The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) confirmed the squad following an intensive 10-day selection and coaching camp, which featured 24 prospects. The selected players will undergo a month-long preparatory camp in Delhi NCR before travelling to Bangladesh for the continental competition. The training programme will focus on batting, bowling, fielding, fitness, conditioning and match strategy. Players were assessed on their performances, fitness levels, technical skills and overall readiness during the selection process. Naresh Tumda, Sanjay Kumar Shah, Debaraj Behera, Ashok Reddy, Praveen Kumar Sharma and Mukesh Kumar Rawat have been selected in the B1 category. The B2 category includes Dunna Venkateshwararao, Rambir Singh, Lokesha, Manish Kumar and Nakula Badanayak, while Durga Rao Tompaki, Sunil Ramesh, Sukhram Majhi, A Ravi, Dinesh Rathva and Deepak complete the squad in the B3 category. Dr Mahantesh G. Kivadasannavar, chairman of CABI, congratulated the selected players and expressed confidence in their preparations. “Congratulations to the 17 players selected to represent India at the Men’s Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026. Each has worked hard to earn a place in the national team. We look forward to seeing them build on India’s proud legacy as they prepare to defend the title. I wish the team every success,” he said. India won the inaugural Blind T20 Asia Cup, hosted by CABI in Kochi in January 2016, defeating Pakistan by 44 runs in the final. The Indian team scored 208/5 before restricting Pakistan to 164, securing the maiden title. India's blind cricket team performance has also been reflected on the international level, as the men's team has won the ICC Blind Cricket World Cup five times across formats. --IANS

stories.headline: Delhi court orders trial against Yasin Malik, six others in money laundering case
stories.title: Delhi court orders trial against Yasin Malik, six others in money laundering case
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 24: A special NIA court in New Delhi has ordered a trial against Yasin Malik, Zahoor Ahmed Shah Watali, Abdul Rashid Sheikh, Shabir Ahmad Shah, Naval Kishore Kapoor, Trison Farms and Construction Pvt Ltd, and Masarat Alam Bhat in Rs 8.9 crore money laundering case, according to a report in The News Mill. According to the report, the accused received the said amount through hawala channels from the Pakistani establishment. The charges stem from a case initially registered by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in 2017. The accused are charged under Sections 120B, 121, and 121A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), as well as Sections 13, 16, 17, 18, 20, 38, 39, and 40 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma, as per the report, ordered the trial to begin, with prosecution evidence recording scheduled to start on November 19. The hearing was conducted in a closed courtroom. Malik appeared via video conferencing from Tihar Jail and denied the charges, stating he will contest the case. In September, the court had framed charges against Malik and six others under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). It is alleged that the accused received funds from the Pakistani establishment and other terrorist organisations to support secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir. The court found sufficient prima facie evidence to charge all seven accused under Section 3 of the PMLA, punishable under Section 4.

The accused are charged under Sections 120B, 121, and 121A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), as well as Sections 13, 16, 17, 18, 20, 38, 39, and 40 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).
Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma, as per the report, ordered the trial to begin, with prosecution evidence recording scheduled to start on November 19.
The hearing was conducted in a closed courtroom.
Malik appeared via video conferencing from Tihar Jail and denied the charges, stating he will contest the case.
In September, the court had framed charges against Malik and six others under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
It is alleged that the accused received funds from the Pakistani establishment and other terrorist organisations to support secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir.
The court found sufficient prima facie evidence to charge all seven accused under Section 3 of the PMLA, punishable under Section 4.
